chunks: Abu Dawood, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, by his chain, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The prayers of the repentant, the fifty [rak'ahs], all of them [are performed] with "Say: He is Allah, [the] One".'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, [the] One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in voluntary prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) states that the fifty rak'ahs of voluntary prayers performed by the repentant (al-awwabin) can all be recited with Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112 of the Quran). This highlights the virtue of Surah Al-Ikhlas and its sufficiency in replacing longer surahs in voluntary prayers. In Shia tradition, this hadith underscores the concept of 'Tasbihat al-Awwabin' and the spiritual weight of Surah Al-Ikhlas, which is often equated with one-third of the Quran, making it highly meritorious for extended voluntary worship.
